title: Eventstream safepoint protocol: fragment checkpoints, function-call alignment, and HTTP compatibility
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design and implement an eventstream 'safepoint' protocol for streaming responses that makes fragment-level checkpoints explicit, preserves function-call / tool-call atomicity across reconnects, and provides an HTTP chunked compatibility adapter for legacy clients. This ticket covers protocol design, server runtime changes, client resume token semantics, tests, rollout plan, and observability hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits periodic safepoint markers in eventstream payloads that are cryptographically lightweight and include monotonic checkpoint IDs
Clients can resume from the last acknowledged safepoint using a resume token with at-least-once delivery semantics and no function-call duplication
HTTP chunked streaming clients (legacy) can use an adapter that maps safepoints into chunk-boundary heuristics and exposes a resume API without breaking existing JSONL boundaries
End-to-end tests simulate network partitions and achieve >= 99.9% successful resume without truncated function-call frames
Console shows per-request resume count, last-safepoint-id, and resumed-from-offset metrics for 30d retention in staging
technical_notes: Safepoint design: short envelope ("SP|<epoch>|<seq>|<hmac>") appended as a discrete SSE event with event: safepoint and data: {base64,resume_token}
Resume token: includes epoch, safepoint_seq, and a 32-byte HMAC keyed by per-deployment signing key. Tokens opaque to clients but verifiable by servers for idempotency checks

Function-call alignment: add a functioncall boundary flag in the stream payload. When reconnect happens, server will replay from the last safepoint and drop any in-flight functioncall whose start was not included in the safepoint to avoid duplication

Compatibility adapter: HTTP chunked shim will inject synthetic safepoints at safe JSONL breakpoints. It will expose an /resume endpoint that accepts the opaque token and negotiates L7 offsets with the runtime
Performance: safepoint events are emitted no more frequently than every 150ms for high-throughput tails, and adaptive backoff increases to 500ms under GC or high CPU
Security: resume tokens signed via KMS; tokens rotate on deploy and we provide a short TTL (24h). Exposed resume endpoint requires customer API key and per-route ACL checks
progress_updates: 2026-02-17: initial protocol proposal reviewed with runtime and SDK teams. Agreed on opaque resume token and safepoint as SSE 'event: safepoint' envelope.
2026-02-20: PoC server emits safepoint events; local client can resume and rehydrate KV cache. Observed 0.6ms median safepoint emit overhead on p4d

2026-02-25: Spike showed function-call duplication risk when safepoint falls mid-toolcall. Decided to include functioncall boundary flag and treat safepoint as atomic only when functioncall flag present.
2026-03-02: Implemented HTTP chunked adapter prototype; it maps flush boundaries to nearest JSONL newline and exposes /resume with token verification. Integration tests passing locally
2026-03-08: Security review prelim with Security team; they requested KMS-backed signing and a token TTL. Ticket updated.

2026-03-10: End-to-end chaos tests in staging show 99.94% resume success across 10k simulated disconnects. Two failure classes remain: long-lived idle connections and buggy intermediaries that buffer SSE events
decision_log: Use SSE 'event: safepoint' instead of modifying existing data frames to preserve backwards compatibility
Make resume tokens opaque and KMS-signed to avoid coupling clients to server internals
Introduce a functioncall boundary flag in the payload rather than a separate control stream to reduce protocol complexity
Provide an HTTP adapter rather than changing legacy client code; adapter can be deployed to edge proxies
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): enable safepoint emit and resume verification for 10% of streaming traffic behind feature flag
Phase 2 (canary): enable HTTP adapter in us-west-2 edge cluster and run 5k heavy-load resumes overnight
Phase 3 (gradual): increase to 50% then 100% over 48h with rollback window and watch resume/error metrics
Phase 4: communicate to SDK teams and publish migration notes for customers using legacy chunked clients
test_plan: Unit tests for token sign/verify and safepoint envelope encoding
Integration: simulate mid-functioncall disconnects and assert no duplicate function calls in delivered output
Chaos: network flaps, TCP resets, and buffered proxy scenarios (Envoy) to validate adapter heuristics
Load: verify safepoint emitter overhead at 2000 rps on dedicated pool
notes_for_review: SDK teams: Please check the resume token handling APIs in your languages. We provide helper to attach resume token to reconnection handshake
Security: Please validate KMS key usage pattern and token TTL; we're currently rotating every deploy which may break long-running dashboards
Platform: need autoscaler rule exception during canary to avoid scale churn when many reconnects happen
